decks.module: License and age and Young applicant conditions

cards.front: Complete the rule: Driving legally in Illinois requires a valid Illinois.
cards.back: Driving legally in Illinois requires a valid Illinois license, and the vehicle’s gross vehicle weight rating determines its license classification.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A basic Illinois license for.
cards.back: A basic Illinois license for driving a car is Class D.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Class D holder may drive a rental.
cards.back: A Class D holder may drive a rental vehicle weighing up to twenty-six thousand pounds within Illinois when carrying personal property belonging to the driver or an immediate family member for a nonbusiness purpose.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For that personal-property rental exception, the rental company.
cards.back: For that personal-property rental exception, the rental company must supply safety-course information that the driver is required to complete successfully.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Special licensing requirements apply to school buses, religious-organization.
cards.back: Special licensing requirements apply to school buses, religious-organization buses, child-care vehicles, for-profit ride-sharing vehicles and vehicles used to transport senior citizens.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Illinois stopped issuing Temporary Visitor Driver’s Licenses on.
cards.back: Illinois stopped issuing Temporary Visitor Driver’s Licenses on July first, two thousand twenty-four; someone previously eligible for one may apply for a standard license.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The general minimum age for an Illinois driver’s.
cards.back: The general minimum age for an Illinois driver’s license is sixteen, subject to the handbook’s listed age-specific conditions.

cards.front: Complete the rule: An applicant aged sixteen or seventeen must finish.
cards.back: An applicant aged sixteen or seventeen must finish state-approved driver education, log fifty hours of practice and pass all three examination components to receive a license.

cards.front: Complete the rule: When a parent or guardian cannot accompany a.
cards.back: When a parent or guardian cannot accompany a minor applicant, a legal guardian or responsible adult older than twenty-one must sign the minor’s consent affidavit.

decks.module: Young applicant conditions and License exemptions

cards.front: Complete the rule: A first-time applicant aged eighteen through twenty who.
cards.back: A first-time applicant aged eighteen through twenty who has never held a license or finished an approved high-school or commercial driver-education program must complete a six-hour course from a state-certified adult driver-education provider.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A driver younger than eighteen cannot drive a.
cards.back: A driver younger than eighteen cannot drive a for-hire property-delivery vehicle or a vehicle requiring a commercial license.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Drivers younger than twenty-one cannot operate for-hire vehicles.
cards.back: Drivers younger than twenty-one cannot operate for-hire vehicles carrying more than ten passengers, commuter vans, religious or school buses, senior-citizen transport vehicles or child-care vehicles.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A new Illinois resident with a valid license.
cards.back: A new Illinois resident with a valid license from elsewhere must obtain the Illinois license within ninety days of moving or before the existing license expires, whichever happens sooner.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A visitor passing through Illinois may drive using.
cards.back: A visitor passing through Illinois may drive using a valid license issued by the visitor’s home state or country.

cards.front: Complete the rule: An out-of-state college or university student in Illinois.
cards.back: An out-of-state college or university student in Illinois, along with that student’s spouse and children, may drive on valid licenses from their home jurisdiction.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Active-duty members of the United States Armed Forces.
cards.back: Active-duty members of the United States Armed Forces and the spouses and dependent children living with them may drive on valid home-state licenses.

cards.front: Complete the rule: An Illinois resident serving in the military outside.
cards.back: An Illinois resident serving in the military outside the United States may use a previously obtained license deferral for the first one hundred twenty days after returning; the returning resident’s spouse and dependent children living with the resident share that provision.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The same one-hundred-twenty-day return provision, with a deferral.
cards.back: The same one-hundred-twenty-day return provision, with a deferral obtained beforehand, covers Illinois-resident civilian employees of the Armed Forces or Defense Department serving abroad and their spouses and dependent children living with them.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A federal employee or service member driving a.
cards.back: A federal employee or service member driving a government-owned or government-leased vehicle on official business does not need an Illinois license for that travel.

cards.front: Complete the rule: An Illinois license is not required to operate.
cards.back: An Illinois license is not required to operate a road machine temporarily on a roadway or a farm tractor between farm buildings and nearby farmland.
cards.memory_hook: Limited farm or road machine use

cards.front: Complete the rule: After a legal name change, apply for a.
cards.back: After a legal name change, apply for a corrected license or identification card within thirty days and present documents linking the new name to the name already recorded.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The name printed on an Illinois credential is.
cards.back: The name printed on an Illinois credential is the full given name and surname established through birth, marriage, Social Security records or another legal action.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Notify the Secretary of State of a move.
cards.back: Notify the Secretary of State of a move within ten days, using a facility visit, online services or a written notice.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Reporting an address change alone does not produce.
cards.back: Reporting an address change alone does not produce a replacement card; getting the new address printed requires a facility visit, acceptable residency documents and the appropriate fee.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Applying for an Illinois license or identification card.
cards.back: Applying for an Illinois license or identification card requires acceptable evidence of legal name, birth date, Social Security number, residence and signature.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The agency compares signatures during identification verification, and.
cards.back: The agency compares signatures during identification verification, and the required document count varies between a first application and a duplicate or correction request.

cards.front: Complete the rule: An applicant must supply a usable mailing address.
cards.back: An applicant must supply a usable mailing address, have a photograph taken and surrender other Illinois licenses, identification cards and instruction permits.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Receiving the requested credential also requires the applicable.
cards.back: Receiving the requested credential also requires the applicable examinations and fee; providing identity documents does not replace those steps.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A first-time REAL ID application needs evidence of.
cards.back: A first-time REAL ID application needs evidence of identity that includes citizenship or lawful status, birth date, Social Security number and signature, plus two documents establishing Illinois residence.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If an identity document uses an earlier legal.
cards.back: If an identity document uses an earlier legal name, the applicant must add documentation showing the reason for the name change, such as a certified marriage record, divorce decree or adoption papers.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A first-time standard Illinois credential needs documentation of.
cards.back: A first-time standard Illinois credential needs documentation of birth date, Social Security number and signature, with one residency document.

cards.front: Complete the rule: One acceptable document can satisfy more.
cards.back: One acceptable document can satisfy more than one of the identification-document groups.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A duplicate or corrected credential requires signature evidence.
cards.back: A duplicate or corrected credential requires signature evidence, and an address printed differently on the replacement also requires residency evidence.

cards.front: Complete the rule: An online duplicate application is available only when.
cards.back: An online duplicate application is available only when the applicant is not changing the address, name or date of birth.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Changing a name, birth date, Social Security number.
cards.back: Changing a name, birth date, Social Security number or gender requires identification linking the previous information with the requested replacement information.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For an applicant younger than sixty, a police.
cards.back: For an applicant younger than sixty, a police report saying the credential was stolen is required to obtain the stolen-card duplicate without a charge.

decks.module: Application documents and Renewal and delivery

cards.front: Complete the rule: The handbook says people older than sixty do.
cards.back: The handbook says people older than sixty do not need a police report to obtain a duplicate license or identification card without a charge.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The agency normally sends a renewal notice roughly.
cards.back: The agency normally sends a renewal notice roughly ninety days before expiry, but renewing on time remains the driver’s responsibility even when no notice arrives.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A two-year or four-year license may be renewed.
cards.back: A two-year or four-year license may be renewed as early as one year before its expiry, while a one-year license may be renewed up to six months early.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The ordinary Illinois license term is four years.
cards.back: The ordinary Illinois license term is four years with expiry on the driver’s birthday, but the handbook lists age-based exceptions.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A license for someone younger than twenty-one.
cards.back: A license for someone younger than twenty-one expires three months after that person’s twenty-first birthday.

cards.front: Complete the rule: For drivers aged eighty-seven or older.
cards.back: For drivers aged eighty-seven or older, the handbook requires license renewal every year.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Standard renewal uses a facility visit with the.
cards.back: Standard renewal uses a facility visit with the current credential, or online services when a PIN renewal notice permits it, together with any required examination, fee and new photograph.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A renewal applicant who cannot surrender the.
cards.back: A renewal applicant who cannot surrender the current credential must provide proof of signature.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Changing an address at renewal requires one residency.
cards.back: Changing an address at renewal requires one residency document for a standard credential and two for a REAL ID credential.
cards.memory_hook: Renewal address standard one REAL two

decks.module: Renewal and delivery and Fraud and medical reporting

cards.front: Complete the rule: Without the current credential, or when making changes.
cards.back: Without the current credential, or when making changes, renewal documentation includes birth date, Social Security number and signature, with residency proof when an address change is requested.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A noncitizen renewing a REAL ID credential.
cards.back: A noncitizen renewing a REAL ID credential must present current evidence of lawful status.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After payment and successful completion of required testing.
cards.back: After payment and successful completion of required testing, the agency issues a secure temporary paper credential valid for ninety days.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The permanent credential is printed centrally after document.
cards.back: The permanent credential is printed centrally after document verification and usually reaches the supplied mailing address within fifteen business days.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A forwarding order or a hold on mail.
cards.back: A forwarding order or a hold on mail service prevents postal delivery of the permanent Illinois credential to that address.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If the permanent credential has not arrived after.
cards.back: If the permanent credential has not arrived after fifteen business days from the facility visit, check its status online or contact the agency.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Credential fraud can lead to arrest, imprisonment for.
cards.back: Credential fraud can lead to arrest, imprisonment for as long as five years and a twelve-month license suspension or revocation.
cards.memory_hook: Fraud risks jail and license loss

cards.front: Complete the rule: False application information, false identity documents, fictitious or.
cards.back: False application information, false identity documents, fictitious or unlawfully altered driving credentials, using someone else’s credential and knowingly lending identity documents for an application in one’s name are listed credential-fraud offenses.
cards.memory_hook: False or borrowed identity is fraud

cards.front: Complete the rule: A license application asks about physical or mental.
cards.back: A license application asks about physical or mental conditions, medicines, other drugs and alcohol that could impair safe driving.

cards.front: Complete the rule: In cases requiring a physician’s Medical Report, present.
cards.back: In cases requiring a physician’s Medical Report, present that completed report to facility staff within ninety days after the physician signs it.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After learning of a condition likely to cause.
cards.back: After learning of a condition likely to cause unconsciousness or loss of safe vehicle control, notify the Secretary of State within ten days; not reporting can lead to cancellation of driving privileges.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Illinois keeps a record of a licensed driver’s.
cards.back: Illinois keeps a record of a licensed driver’s traffic violations and crashes, including convictions received in other states.

cards.back: A driver may obtain a paid copy of the driving record through online services, selected facilities or a written request.
